---
title: "Install Quarto"
---

## Why Quarto?

Quarto is what turns your `.qmd` files into finished documents. You write prose and code in
one file, press render, and Quarto runs the code and drops the results, tables, and charts
into place. Your final White Paper is a Quarto document.

It is also the piece students most often think they have installed when they do not.

:::{.callout-important}
## The VS Code extension is not the program

There are two separate things with the same name, and you need both:

1. **Quarto**, the program. It does the actual work. You download it from quarto.org and
   install it like any other application. **This page.**
2. **The Quarto extension** for VS Code. It adds the Render button, the preview pane, and
   syntax highlighting. It is a front end for the program above.

Installing the extension does not install the program. If you searched for "Quarto" inside
VS Code's Extensions panel and clicked Install, you have the extension only, and `quarto
render` will still fail.
:::

---

## What you'll install

1. **Quarto** itself, the command line program
2. The **Quarto extension** for VS Code, if you do not already have it

Install R first if you have not: [Install R](install-r.qmd). Quarto needs R in order to run
the R code inside your documents.

---

## Step 1: Install Quarto

### Windows

1. Go to [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
2. Click the download button for **Windows**. You get a `.msi` file.
3. Run it and accept every default.

The installer adds Quarto to your PATH, which is what lets you type `quarto` in a terminal.

### macOS

1. Go to [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
2. Click the download button for **macOS**. You get a `.pkg` file.
3. Run it and accept every default.

### Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

Download the `.deb` from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/), then:

```bash
sudo dpkg -i quarto-*-linux-amd64.deb
```

---

## Step 2: Close your terminal and open a new one

This step is not optional, and skipping it is the most common reason Quarto looks broken
five minutes after a successful install.

A terminal only learns about programs that existed when it opened. If you had a terminal
open while the installer ran, that terminal has never heard of Quarto and never will. In VS
Code, click the bin icon on the terminal panel to close it, then **Terminal, New Terminal**.

---

## Step 3: Verify with `quarto check`

In a new terminal, run:

```bash
quarto check
```

`quarto check` is Quarto's own self test. It checks itself, then goes looking for the other
pieces of your toolchain and prints a line for each. You want green check marks under
**Quarto** and under **R**.

:::{.callout-note}
## On Windows, `R --version` failing does not mean R is broken

If you type `R --version` in a terminal on Windows you will probably see "not recognized",
even with R installed and working perfectly. The R installer does not add R to your PATH,
and it does not need to: Quarto finds R through the Windows registry instead.

Trust `quarto check`. It is the answer to "is my setup working", and `R --version` is not.
:::

---

## Step 4: Install the VS Code extension

Open VS Code, open the Extensions view (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+X`), search for **Quarto** by
Posit, and click **Install**.

If you cloned the [course workspace](workspace-setup.qmd), it is already in the recommended
set and VS Code will offer it to you.

---

## Step 5: Render something

Open any `.qmd` file, such as
[`00-check-your-setup.qmd`](../starters/00-check-your-setup.qmd), and either click
**Render** at the top of the editor or run:

```bash
quarto render 00-check-your-setup.qmd
```

**You should see:** a stream of output ending in `Output created:` and a new `.html` file
beside your `.qmd`.

---

## Common first-time issues

### `quarto: command not found` or `'quarto' is not recognized`

Almost always Step 2. Close the terminal, open a new one, and try again. If it still fails
after a fresh terminal, the install did not finish, so run the installer again.

### `quarto check` says R was not found

Quarto found itself but not R. Install R first ([Install R](install-r.qmd)), then close and
reopen your terminal and run `quarto check` again.

### The Render button appears but does nothing

You have the extension and not the program. Go back to Step 1.

### `ERROR: Failed to spawn 'Rscript'`

Same cause as above, seen from the other side: Quarto is trying to run the R code in your
document and cannot find R. Install R, then reopen the terminal.

### Render fails with a YAML error

The `---` block must be the very first thing in the file, with nothing above it, not even a
blank line.

### I already have RStudio, am I done?

No. RStudio ships its own private copy of Quarto that only RStudio can see. It is not on
your PATH and VS Code cannot use it. Install Quarto properly with Step 1.
